messages:
Maria V: Heads-up: nightly eval surfaced a large quality regression for the int8 build of llama3-small using the new 'bimodal-scaling' quant profile. ROUGE-L down ~12% on summarization promptset, a bunch of hallucinations.
Ajay R: ugh. is this headlined in the nightly report link?
Maria V: nightly-evals-bot reported it, yes. link: https://ci.example.com/runs/2293102468 (fails on summarizer_suite/long-docs)
nightly-evals-bot: [automated] job failed: summarizer_suite/long-docs | delta_ROUGE_L = -12.3 | affected_models = [llama3-small-int8-bimodal]
Sam L: I can repro locally with the saved inputs. some outputs are truncated / nonsensical. sharing a minimal repro command:

```
python tools/run_eval.py --model=llama3-small-int8-bimodal --prompts=tests/inputs/long-docs.jsonl --batch=4 --seed=42
```

Got several responses where the model repeats "Error:" then dumps short unrelated sentences.
Ajay R: logs? any NaNs or infs in the logits during generation?
Sam L: saw a few NaNs in the step logs. snippet:

```
[2024-11-02T03:14:12Z] step=12 token=345 logit=nan
[2024-11-02T03:14:12Z] step=12 kv_cache_ok=false
```

Also noticed scale factors > 1e6 for a few channels when using the bimodal scaler.
Priyanka S: bimodal-scaling was added to handle activation skew, but we haven't rolled it across all checkpoints. could be an instability with per-channel scale + grouped quant bins.
Kevin H: can we diff the calibration tables between per-layer and per-channel runs? maybe the per-channel calibration is overfitting to outliers.
Maria V: attaching the quant config we used:

```
quant_config:
  mode: per_channel
  scale_method: bimodal
  bin_count: 128
  clip_pct: 0.999
  calib_samples: 2048
```

We had switched clip_pct from 0.9995 -> 0.999 in the nightly to reduce tail sensitivity.
Ajay R: that change could explain more extreme scale values. lower clip_pct -> tighter clip -> larger scale for remaining values.
Sam L: quick experiment: re-ran calibration with clip_pct: 0.9995 and per_layer mode. ROUGE drop disappears on my local subset. results:
- per_channel + 0.999: ROUGE_L delta -12%
- per_layer + 0.9995: ROUGE_L delta -0.8%
Priyanka S: ok looks like an interaction between per_channel + lower clip. two hypotheses:
1) bimodal scaling amplifies rare channel outliers when clip_pct is lower -> numeric instability (NaNs)
2) calibration sample skew: some extreme batches in nightly changed calibration stats
Kevin H: action plan suggestion:
- revert nightly to using per_layer + clip_pct=0.9995 for canary (low risk)
- re-run a dedicated calibration sweep (per_layer/per_channel x clip_pct 0.999/0.9995 x bin_count 64/128) on the failing model with fixed seed
- add quick NaN/inf detection post-calib to fail early
Maria V: sounds good. I'll open a backfill job and schedule the sweep. also bump the alert severity so oncall sees it.
ci-bot: created ticket CI-4821: "int8 bimodal calibration instability - triage" and triggered backfill job backfill/2293102468-calib-sweep
Ajay R: I'll own the calibration sweep matrix. will post artifacts and calibration tables.
Sam L: I'll prepare a small set of golden prompts and add a smoke check to nightly that runs on the golden set before promoting the profile.
Priyanka S: if sweep confirms per_channel is fragile, we should default to per_layer for new models until we get robust binning and clipping heuristics.
Maria V: agreed. follow-ups: Ajay -> upload cal tables + diff; Sam -> add golden smoke check; Priyanka -> prepare rollback PR for canary; Kevin -> add NaN gating to runtime. target to have canary reverted within 2 hours.
Kevin H: noted. ping me in #eng-oncall when canary is live.
Maria V: thanks team. will update thread with links to sweep outputs. :thumbsup:
